spans.s: अपोढ. See s. v., p. 56.

अपोढ अपोढ, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. rt. वह् with
अप), carried off, removed, taken away.

अपोच्छद् अपोच्छद् (अप-उद्-छद्), cl. 10.
P. A. -छादयति, -ते, -यितुम्, to uncover.

अपोत्कृष् अपोत्-कृष् (अप-उद्-कृष्), cl. 1. 6.
P. A. -कर्षति, -ते, -क्रिषति, -ते, -कर्ष्टुम्,
-क्रष्टुम्, to separate, disjoin.

अपोदक अपोदक (˚प-उद्˚) अस्, आ, अम्, water-
less, water-tight; not watery, not fluid; (इका), f. a
pot-herb, Basella Rubra or Lucida.

अपोदि अपोद्-इ (अप-उद्-इ), cl. 2. P. -एति,
-तुम्, to go away altogether, to give way, to with-
draw.

अपोद्-इत्य, अस्, आ, अम्, to be completely gone
away from or left.

अपोद्धार्य अपोद्-धार्य, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. rt. हृ
with अप and उद्), liable to have something taken
away.
अपोनपात् अपो-नपात्, &c. See under अप्.

अपोभ् अपोभ् (अप-उभ्), cl. 6. P., Ved. अपो-
भति, -ओम्भति, -भितुम्, to bind, fetter.

अपोर्णु अपोर्णु (अप-ऊर्णु), cl. 2. P. A.
अपोर्णौति, -णोति, -णुते, -णवितुम्, -णुवितुम्, to
uncover, to unveil, to open; A. to uncover one's self.

अपोष् अपोष् (अप-उष्), cl. 1. P., Ved.
अपोषति, अपोच्छति, to dispel darkness (said of the
dawn).

अपोह् अपोह् (अप-ऊह्), cl. 1. P. A. अपोहति,
-ते, -हितुम्, to strip off, to push away, to frighten
away; to remove, to heal (sickness); A. to keep
away from one's self, to avoid, to give up; (in dis-
putation) to object, to deny, to reason, argue.

अपोह, अस्, m. or अपोहन, अम्, n. pushing away,
removing; removal of doubt by the exercise of the
reasoning faculty; reasoning, arguing.

अपोहनीय or अपोह्य, अस्, आ, अम्, to be taken
away, or removed, or expiated.

अपोहित, अस्, आ, अम्, taken away, removed; estab-
lished by reason.

आपोक्लिम आपोक्लिम, अस्, m., in astronomy
= Gr. ἀπόκλιμα

आपोमय आपो-मय, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. आपस्, nom.
pl. of अप्, q. v.), consisting of water.
—आपो-मात्रा,
f. the subtle elementary principle of water.
—आपो-
मूर्ति, इस्, m., N. of a deity under Manu Svārociṣa,
one of the seven Ṛṣis of the tenth Manvantara.

आपोशान आपोशान, अस्, m., N. of a kind of
prayer spoken before and after eating; perhaps con-
tracted from आपो ऽशान, ‘drink the water,’ with
which words the prayer began.
अपोब्ध, अस्, आ, अम्, bound.
अपोम्भन, अम्, n. binding, a bond, fetter.
